page1.text:
It was a beautiful, moonlit night.
I was just enjoying the sight with my father, Kiritsugu Emiya.
It was winter, but it wasn't very cold.
On the veranda it was just a little chilly, the perfect weather to watch the moon.

page2.text:
Kiritsugu didn't go outside much anymore.
He rarely went out, and he spent most of his time lounging around the house.
...Every time I recall this, I still feel regret.
Why didn't I realize that he was acting the way any creature does when they know their time is almost up?

page3.text:
"When I was a boy, I wanted to be a hero of justice."
He blurted it out, just out of nowhere.
My father, who already seemed like a hero of justice in my eyes, said that as if he were reflecting on a memory.

page4.text:
"What, you wanted to? So you gave up on it?"
I asked, unable to completely hide my disappointment.
Kiritsugu smiled apologetically, and looked up at the distant moon.

page5.text:
"Unfortunately, yes. You can only be a hero for so long. It gets harder to call yourself one as you grow up. I wish I'd found that out earlier."
That made sense to me.
I wasn't sure why, but if Kiritsugu said it, then it had to be true.

page6.text:
"Oh. Well, that's too bad."
"Yes. It really is too bad."
Kiritsugu nodded in agreement.
So I just kind of blurted something out, as if it were a natural thing to say.
"Okay. If you can't do it, then I'll do it for you.
You can't do anything because you're an adult, but I can. You can leave your dream to me."

page7.text: Because I'll make it a reality.

page8.text:
The bold promise made my father smile.
His face said everything I needed to know.
Kiritsugu made a long, contented sigh, and whispered,
"Ah...that's a relief."
There, he closed his eyes, and so too his life came to a close.

page10.text:
There's no way I could forget.
I never talk about this, but I still remember it.
Ten years ago, a man saved me from a fire.

page11.text:
He said 'thank you' as he picked up the child who was unconscious, covered in burns, and on the verge of dying.
That he was glad to have found him.
He smiled, as if thanking someone, saying that he was glad to have been able to rescue at least one person.

page12.text:
...The emotion that I felt then is engraved in my mind.
Nobody saved me.
I couldn't save anyone.
In the midst of that, I was the only person that was saved, and there was only one person who saved me.
That's why I decided to be like him.

page13.text:
I wanted to become a hero of justice that saves people and doesn't let anyone die.
Even if it was a childish fantasy, I dreamt of doing so.

page14.text:
...And then...
Kiritsugu, who was the embodiment of my dream himself, left behind his dream of becoming something like that and died peacefully.

page15.text:
It's only natural for a child to follow in their father's footsteps.
Shirou Emiya must become a hero of justice and save someone like me.

page16.text:
Yes, I strongly swore so as a child.
Shirou Emiya would fulfill the dream on behalf of the man that he admired more than anyone else.

page17.text:
...But, I don't really know to be honest.
If the way that I think is correct.
Where that way of thinking comes from.
What I can do as an amateur.
How to make the dream of making everyone happy that Kiritsugu would often mention, which is itself as far-fetched as Magic, come true.

page18.text:
...Oh, and...
What I can do as a Master now... There's too many things to think about that my head feels like it's about to burst...

page19.text:
...
A nostalgic dream flitters through my mind, and then I wake.
The bright morning light comes in through the window.
It's chilly in my room and my body feels it despite a blanket wrapped around me.

page20.text:
"...Damn. I fell asleep here again."
I shake my head and change from my coveralls to my school uniform.
It's a bit before 6 AM.
Sakura is probably already up and making breakfast.

page21.text:
I make my way out to the yard and take in the morning air.
Ah, it's a good morning.
Though I'm preoccupied by the thought of the three girls also staying here.

page22.text:
"...Well, not exactly. More like two girls."
I'd be hard-pressed to call Fuji-nee a girl.
Anyway, now...
